observations.scope: There is a low level of geological confidence associated with Inferred Mineral Resources and there is no certainty that further exploration work will result in the determination of Indicated Mineral Resources or that the Life of Mine Production Target itself (or the forecast financial information) will be realised. Overview Australian Rare Earths Limited (AR3 or the Company) has completed a Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) for its flagship 100%- owned Koppamurra Rare Earths Project (Koppamurra or the Project) in South Australia, delivering very strong project economics that firmly establish Koppamurra as one of the most compelling rare earth development opportunities in Australia: • Exceptional returns on attractively low capital spend: Base Case after-tax NPV₈ of A$858 million and after-tax IRR of 99% on initial capital expenditure (CAPEX) of just A$178 million — a capital efficiency ratio rarely seen in the resources sector and a clear signal of the value embedded in this asset. • Strategic exposure to high-value rare earths with rapid payback: Capital payback in just 0.9 years post-tax, with annual production of Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) feedstock containing approximately 1,860 tonnes of Total Rare Earth Oxides (TREO) including a strategically critical suite of magnet rare earths — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — along with yttrium, gadolinium, samarium and lutetium. All are increasingly critical to Western supply chains, with most subject to Chinese export controls. • Significant upside beyond the PFS mine plan: The PFS draws on a maiden Ore Reserve of 26Mt at 920ppm TREO and processing capacity of 3Mtpa for an initial 12-year mine life.

Overview Australian Rare Earths Limited (AR3 or the Company) has completed a Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) for its flagship 100%- owned Koppamurra Rare Earths Project (Koppamurra or the Project) in South Australia, delivering very strong project economics that firmly establish Koppamurra as one of the most compelling rare earth development opportunities in Australia: • Exceptional returns on attractively low capital spend: Base Case after-tax NPV₈ of A$858 million and after-tax IRR of 99% on initial capital expenditure (CAPEX) of just A$178 million — a capital efficiency ratio rarely seen in the resources sector and a clear signal of the value embedded in this asset. • Strategic exposure to high-value rare earths with rapid payback: Capital payback in just 0.9 years post-tax, with annual production of Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) feedstock containing approximately 1,860 tonnes of Total Rare Earth Oxides (TREO) including a strategically critical suite of magnet rare earths — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — along with yttrium, gadolinium, samarium and lutetium. All are increasingly critical to Western supply chains, with most subject to Chinese export controls. • Significant upside beyond the PFS mine plan: The PFS draws on a maiden Ore Reserve of 26Mt at 920ppm TREO and processing capacity of 3Mtpa for an initial 12-year mine life.

Overview Australian Rare Earths Limited (AR3 or the Company) has completed a Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) for its flagship 100%- owned Koppamurra Rare Earths Project (Koppamurra or the Project) in South Australia, delivering very strong project economics that firmly establish Koppamurra as one of the most compelling rare earth development opportunities in Australia: • Exceptional returns on attractively low capital spend: Base Case after-tax NPV₈ of A$858 million and after-tax IRR of 99% on initial capital expenditure (CAPEX) of just A$178 million — a capital efficiency ratio rarely seen in the resources sector and a clear signal of the value embedded in this asset. • Strategic exposure to high-value rare earths with rapid payback: Capital payback in just 0.9 years post-tax, with annual production of Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) feedstock containing approximately 1,860 tonnes of Total Rare Earth Oxides (TREO) including a strategically critical suite of magnet rare earths — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — along with yttrium, gadolinium, samarium and lutetium. All are increasingly critical to Western supply chains, with most subject to Chinese export controls. • Significant upside beyond the PFS mine plan: The PFS draws on a maiden Ore Reserve of 26Mt at 920ppm TREO and processing capacity of 3Mtpa for an initial 12-year mine life. The broader resource and substantial Exploration Target provides potential to materially extend mine life beyond the initial PFS case in a capital efficient manner.

observations.scope: Flowsheet Development The Koppamurra ore is a clay-hosted rare earth element (REE) deposit characterised by a combination of ionically adsorbed, acid-soluble and refractory rare earth mineralisation. Early metallurgical assessment identified sulphuric acid, with MgSO4 as the desorption agent, as a feasible lixiviant system, with an optimal leaching pH of approximately 2.2. The ore contains high proportions of swelling clay minerals, particularly smectite and mixed-layer illite/smectite, which created difficulties with solid-liquid separation following slurry leaching.

Turner & Townsend (T&T) were engaged by AR3 to develop the estimates with information provided by AR3 and WGA’s engineering design, adopting an agreed work breakdown structure (WBS). • Vendor budget pricing was sourced for the major equipment packages including filters, heap leach irrigation system, conveyors, radial stacker and thickener. • Mechanical equipment, earthworks, concrete, steel, pipework and electrical pricing was benchmarked to cost data from similar mining projects. • Indirect costs including temporary construction facilities, EPCM, spares, first fills, laboratory expenses, freight and contingency are factored based on in-house data. • In accordance with AUSIMM, contingency of 25% has been allowed for, consistent with the level of engineering design for Class 4 studies. Capital Cost Estimation (CAPEX) The Class 4 capital cost estimate for the Koppamurra Project, including the 25% contingency is A$178 million.

An after-tax IRR of 99% against an initial capital requirement of A$178 million represents a value creation profile that investors in resources development very rarely encounter at the PFS stage.

observations.scope: The Koppamurra mineralisation represents an unusual sediment-hosted ionic clay rare earth system formed through weathering, sedimentary transport and geochemical enrichment linked to far-field granitic source rocks of the Lachlan Orogen. The ionic adsorption characteristics of the mineralisation mean rare earths are easily liberated using a mild acidic solution with magnesium sulphate as a desorption agent — the basis for the heap leach flowsheet that drives the project's low-cost profile. Figure 2 Typical Cross Section - Koppamurra Why the rare earth composition matters: The resource contains a magnet rare earth element (MRE) component accounting for 25% of total TREO, encompassing all four key magnet REEs.

observations.scope: ASX Release 13 July 2026 Cummins Range Metallurgical Program Delivers Strongest Results Engage with this announcement at the RareX investor hub. Highlights • SGS Lakefield flotation testwork achieves a 9.5x TREO upgrade to 25.15% grade from 2.85% TREO feed — a positive result achieved for Cummins Range high-grade ore. • Rougher concentrate demonstrates strong recovery of 74.6% TREO at 6.41% grade (F8), providing a proven foundation for cleaner circuit optimisation. • Advanced TIMA and laser ablation mineralogical characterisation identifies monazite liberation grind size as the primary constraint on recovery, providing a clear technical roadmap for next-stage optimisation through finer and staged grinding. • Laser ablation confirms highly elevated gallium (Ga: 5,538 ppm) concentrations within the monazite phase, validating the strategic importance of the Ga by-product pathway. • Gega Elements confirms near-complete extraction of Ga via optimised acid bake and water leaching methodology. • Gallium co-precipitation during PLS purification could be a potential enrichment step, creating a concentrated Ga-Ge intermediate cake; ion exchange (IX) resin subsequently demonstrated >93% Ga recovery from the purified PLS. • High extractions of REEs (71–84%), Sc (89–93%) and Nb observed during GEGA leaching, opening potential for an integrated multi-element recovery flowsheet from a single acid bake step. • Phosphate-focused nano-P collaboration with Biological Inputs under review; strong agronomic results at laboratory scale pending validation. RareX Limited (ASX: REE, REEO – RareX, or the Company) is pleased to advise that recent metallurgical test work has delivered positive flotation beneficiation results for its 100%-owned Cummins Range Rare Earths & Phosphate Project in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia, while confirming a viable extraction pathway for gallium (Ga).

observations.scope: Key agronomic highlights from the trial program — conducted at Agronomy Solutions, South Australia, across wheat, tomato and bean crops in Calcarosol and Vertisol soils — include: • Nano-P derived from Cummins Range rock phosphate outperformed MAP across multiple crop-soil combinations at comparable or lower application rates. • PUE, expressed as equivalent MAP performance, increased by up to approximately 400% in select treatments under high P-fixation conditions. • Strong responses were recorded in both calcareous South Australian soils and northern Australian Vertisols — both soils where conventional P fertilisers underperform. • Wheat trials in Calcarosol: basal nano-P at 2.2–5 kg P/ha delivered yields equivalent to 8–28 kg P/ha as MAP, implying PUE gains of ~265–461%. Preliminary synthesis data indicates that REEs remain largely in the bio-leach residue following nano-P extraction, suggesting potential upgrading benefits for downstream RE, Ga and Sc processing — consistent with the integrated flowsheet concept being explored across the three workstreams. A second round of nano-P synthesis from finer-grind (100 µm) Cummins Range material is underway.

observations.scope: Key agronomic highlights from the trial program — conducted at Agronomy Solutions, South Australia, across wheat, tomato and bean crops in Calcarosol and Vertisol soils — include: • Nano-P derived from Cummins Range rock phosphate outperformed MAP across multiple crop-soil combinations at comparable or lower application rates. • PUE, expressed as equivalent MAP performance, increased by up to approximately 400% in select treatments under high P-fixation conditions. • Strong responses were recorded in both calcareous South Australian soils and northern Australian Vertisols — both soils where conventional P fertilisers underperform. • Wheat trials in Calcarosol: basal nano-P at 2.2–5 kg P/ha delivered yields equivalent to 8–28 kg P/ha as MAP, implying PUE gains of ~265–461%. observations.scope: Highlights • SGS Lakefield flotation testwork achieves a 9.5x TREO upgrade to 25.15% grade from 2.85% TREO feed — a positive result achieved for Cummins Range high-grade ore. • Rougher concentrate demonstrates strong recovery of 74.6% TREO at 6.41% grade (F8), providing a proven foundation for cleaner circuit optimisation. • Advanced TIMA and laser ablation mineralogical characterisation identifies monazite liberation grind size as the primary constraint on recovery, providing a clear technical roadmap for next-stage optimisation through finer and staged grinding. • Laser ablation confirms highly elevated gallium (Ga: 5,538 ppm) concentrations within the monazite phase, validating the strategic importance of the Ga by-product pathway. • Gega Elements confirms near-complete extraction of Ga via optimised acid bake and water leaching methodology. • Gallium co-precipitation during PLS purification could be a potential enrichment step, creating a concentrated Ga-Ge intermediate cake; ion exchange (IX) resin subsequently demonstrated >93% Ga recovery from the purified PLS. • High extractions of REEs (71–84%), Sc (89–93%) and Nb observed during GEGA leaching, opening potential for an integrated multi-element recovery flowsheet from a single acid bake step. • Phosphate-focused nano-P collaboration with Biological Inputs under review; strong agronomic results at laboratory scale pending validation. RareX Limited (ASX: REE, REEO – RareX, or the Company) is pleased to advise that recent metallurgical test work has delivered positive flotation beneficiation results for its 100%-owned Cummins Range Rare Earths & Phosphate Project in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia, while confirming a viable extraction pathway for gallium (Ga). Test work was resumed after RareX secured a mining heritage protection agreement with the Jaru native title holders, and the subsequent award of the mining lease for Cummins Range.

observations.scope: Highlights • SGS Lakefield flotation testwork achieves a 9.5x TREO upgrade to 25.15% grade from 2.85% TREO feed — a positive result achieved for Cummins Range high-grade ore. • Rougher concentrate demonstrates strong recovery of 74.6% TREO at 6.41% grade (F8), providing a proven foundation for cleaner circuit optimisation. • Advanced TIMA and laser ablation mineralogical characterisation identifies monazite liberation grind size as the primary constraint on recovery, providing a clear technical roadmap for next-stage optimisation through finer and staged grinding. • Laser ablation confirms highly elevated gallium (Ga: 5,538 ppm) concentrations within the monazite phase, validating the strategic importance of the Ga by-product pathway. • Gega Elements confirms near-complete extraction of Ga via optimised acid bake and water leaching methodology. • Gallium co-precipitation during PLS purification could be a potential enrichment step, creating a concentrated Ga-Ge intermediate cake; ion exchange (IX) resin subsequently demonstrated >93% Ga recovery from the purified PLS. • High extractions of REEs (71–84%), Sc (89–93%) and Nb observed during GEGA leaching, opening potential for an integrated multi-element recovery flowsheet from a single acid bake step. • Phosphate-focused nano-P collaboration with Biological Inputs under review; strong agronomic results at laboratory scale pending validation. RareX Limited (ASX: REE, REEO – RareX, or the Company) is pleased to advise that recent metallurgical test work has delivered positive flotation beneficiation results for its 100%-owned Cummins Range Rare Earths & Phosphate Project in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia, while confirming a viable extraction pathway for gallium (Ga). Test work was resumed after RareX secured a mining heritage protection agreement with the Jaru native title holders, and the subsequent award of the mining lease for Cummins Range.

observations.scope: Background and Project Context RareX has conducted extensive, though intermittent, metallurgical testwork on Cummins Range ore over a number of years. The most significant results were previously achieved at Baotou Mengrong Fine Materials (BTMR), a specialist Chinese laboratory, which demonstrated a 20x TREO upgrade with flotation recoveries of up to 48.74% on approximately 1% TREO head-grade material1. Following changes to China's critical mineral export and research collaboration policies, RareX was unable to continue work with BTMR from 2024 onwards.

observations.scope: Prior Australian beneficiation testwork undertaken by Auralia Metallurgy, ALS and ANSTO yielded upgrade factors generally in the range of 2–3x2, 3, significantly below the outcomes achieved with BTMR. The current SGS Lakefield program, leveraging that laboratory's deep expertise in RE flotation chemistry has produced the most encouraging results to date, and provides a strong technical foundation from which to optimise toward commercially viable concentrate grades and recoveries. Cummins Range Composite Sample (CRCS-10), grading at 2.85% total rare earth oxide (TREO), was used as the primary composite for both the SGS Lakefield and Gega Elements programs.

observations.scope: Prior Australian beneficiation testwork undertaken by Auralia Metallurgy, ALS and ANSTO yielded upgrade factors generally in the range of 2–3x2, 3, significantly below the outcomes achieved with BTMR. The current SGS Lakefield program, leveraging that laboratory's deep expertise in RE flotation chemistry has produced the most encouraging results to date, and provides a strong technical foundation from which to optimise toward commercially viable concentrate grades and recoveries. Cummins Range Composite Sample (CRCS-10), grading at 2.85% total rare earth oxide (TREO), was used as the primary composite for both the SGS Lakefield and Gega Elements programs.

observations.scope: T H E F U T U R E O F A U S T R A L I A N H E A V Y R A R E E A R T H S KEY OPPORTUNITIES Opportunities identified are not isolated studies, however still form part of a broader strategy to develop North Stanmore as a technically differentiated rare earth operation. The combination of circular water management, digital process intelligence, advanced flotation systems and selective critical mineral recovery have the potential to create project specific intellectual property while improving operating performance, reducing environmental impact and enhancing long term project value. The PFS identifies several opportunities to further enhance Project value during the DFS phase and beyond.

observations.scope: Advanced Flotation Reagent Development A further opportunity exists to develop flotation reagent strategies specifically tailored to clay hosted rare earth ores and recycled water operation. Most commercial flotation reagent suites have been developed for conventional mineral systems and may not be fully optimised for the unique mineralogical and water quality conditions expected at North Stanmore. Systematic optimisation of collectors, depressants, dispersants and water conditioning approaches has the potential to improve recovery, increase concentrate grade and reduce reagent consumption.

observations.scope: Indicative deportment results show that these secondary phosphate groups host most of the target rare earth value. This mineralogy supports flotation-led beneficiation and selective leaching strategy. • The PFS mining study pit optimisation work has confirmed a ≥300 ppm TREO economic reporting cutoff, which aligns with the MRE economic reporting cutoff grade. The Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) is hosted within weathered regolith developed above the North Stanmore alkaline intrusion, with rare earth mineralisation occurring predominantly within a relatively flat- lying, saprolite-rich horizon beneath transported cover.

observations.scope: V T M P R E - F E A S I B I L I T Y S T U D Y – A U G U S T 2 0 2 6 Selective Recovery of Scandium and Gallium Scandium and Gallium represent the most attractive byproduct opportunities currently identified within the North Stanmore resource and will be assessed independently from the primary rare earth processing circuit. The objective is to determine whether these elements can be recovered from existing process streams with minimal additional complexity while preserving the economics and operability of the main rare earth flowsheet. The initial focus will be on understanding where these elements report during processing, whether to flotation concentrates, leach solutions, residues or impurity streams.

observations.scope: The Scoping Study was prepared by Sedgman Pty Ltd (“Sedgman”), with Snowden Optiro providing the mine design and scheduling work and SRK Consulting (“SRK”) responsible for the Mineral Resource Estimate underpinning the Study. The Scoping Study outlines a potential large-scale rare earths development pathway based on conventional open-pit mining, beneficiation and downstream hydrometallurgical processing to produce a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). The Study is based on an 8.0 Mtpa processing design basis and evaluates the development of Jupiter’s near-surface rare earth mineralisation, with the Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources.

observations.scope: The Scoping Study was prepared by Sedgman Pty Ltd (“Sedgman”), with Snowden Optiro providing the mine design and scheduling work and SRK Consulting (“SRK”) responsible for the Mineral Resource Estimate underpinning the Study. The Scoping Study outlines a potential large-scale rare earths development pathway based on conventional open-pit mining, beneficiation and downstream hydrometallurgical processing to produce a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). The Study is based on an 8.0 Mtpa processing design basis and evaluates the development of Jupiter’s near-surface rare earth mineralisation, with the Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources.

Summary • Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%- owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). • Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160 Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026. • Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. observations.scope: Executive Summary • Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%- owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). • Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160 Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026. • Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. 2

announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. 2

ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026. • Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. 2

observations.scope: Executive Summary • Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%- owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). • Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160 Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026. • Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. 2

observations.scope: Executive Summary • Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%- owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). • Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160 Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026. • Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. 2

Processing Flowsheet The Jupiter Scoping Study processing facilities are designed for a nominal 8.0 Mtpa plant feed rate and comprise two principal stages: beneficiation of run-of-mine material to produce a rare earth-enriched intermediate concentrate, followed by hydrometallurgical treatment to produce mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC). The proposed processing flowsheet comprises the following principal stages: Stage 1 – Beneficiation • Scrubbing and screening: Run-of-mine material is scrubbed to disperse clay and separate oversize material, which is ground and returned to the circuit. • Magnetic separation: Iron-bearing minerals are separated from the feed, producing magnetite- rich and hematite-rich streams and reducing the mass reporting to flotation. • Flotation: Rare earth-bearing phosphate minerals are recovered and upgraded to produce an intermediate rare earth concentrate, while rejecting the majority of the original feed mass. • Concentrate washing and dewatering: The intermediate concentrate is washed and dewatered in preparation for downstream hydrometallurgical treatment.

Processing Flowsheet The Jupiter Scoping Study processing facilities are designed for a nominal 8.0 Mtpa plant feed rate and comprise two principal stages: beneficiation of run-of-mine material to produce a rare earth-enriched intermediate concentrate, followed by hydrometallurgical treatment to produce mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC). The proposed processing flowsheet comprises the following principal stages: Stage 1 – Beneficiation • Scrubbing and screening: Run-of-mine material is scrubbed to disperse clay and separate oversize material, which is ground and returned to the circuit. • Magnetic separation: Iron-bearing minerals are separated from the feed, producing magnetite- rich and hematite-rich streams and reducing the mass reporting to flotation. • Flotation: Rare earth-bearing phosphate minerals are recovered and upgraded to produce an intermediate rare earth concentrate, while rejecting the majority of the original feed mass. • Concentrate washing and dewatering: The intermediate concentrate is washed and dewatered in preparation for downstream hydrometallurgical treatment.

observations.scope: Processing Flowsheet The Jupiter Scoping Study processing facilities are designed for a nominal 8.0 Mtpa plant feed rate and comprise two principal stages: beneficiation of run-of-mine material to produce a rare earth-enriched intermediate concentrate, followed by hydrometallurgical treatment to produce mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC). The proposed processing flowsheet comprises the following principal stages: Stage 1 – Beneficiation • Scrubbing and screening: Run-of-mine material is scrubbed to disperse clay and separate oversize material, which is ground and returned to the circuit. • Magnetic separation: Iron-bearing minerals are separated from the feed, producing magnetite- rich and hematite-rich streams and reducing the mass reporting to flotation. • Flotation: Rare earth-bearing phosphate minerals are recovered and upgraded to produce an intermediate rare earth concentrate, while rejecting the majority of the original feed mass. • Concentrate washing and dewatering: The intermediate concentrate is washed and dewatered in preparation for downstream hydrometallurgical treatment. Stage 2 – Hydrometallurgical Processing • Sulphuric acid baking: The beneficiated concentrate is mixed with sulphuric acid and heated to convert the contained rare earth minerals into a form suitable for subsequent leaching. • Water leaching: The baked material is leached with water to dissolve the rare earths into solution. • Oxidation and staged impurity removal: The leach solution undergoes oxidation and staged neutralisation to remove impurities, including iron, aluminium and phosphorus, while retaining the rare earths in solution. • MREC precipitation: The purified solution is treated to precipitate the contained rare earths as MREC, which is then separated and prepared as the final product assumed in the Scoping Study Base Case.

observations.scope: Further evaluation work and appropriate studies are required before Critica will be in a position to estimate any Ore Reserves or to assess whether Critica may be able to provide any assurance of an economic development case. The Scoping Study Production Target is based on part of the Jupiter JORC 2012 compliant Mineral Resource Estimate announced by the Company on 12 October 2026. The Production Target comprises approximately 107 Mt of scheduled plant feed, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant-feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling, of which approximately 97% is derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and approximately 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources.

observations.scope: The iron concentrate represents a potential additional product stream from the Jupiter beneficiation flowsheet; however, no revenue or value from iron is included in the Scoping Study Base Case. MREC Pricing The Scoping Study Base Case assumes a gross MREC basket value of approximately US$52,800/t MREC (US$52.80/kg MREC) and 75% payability against that gross basket value. observations.scope: Cut-off grade The Mineral Resource is reported above a 200 ppm TREO-Ce for open pit method of mining and value of REO in individual operation ISR cell for covering of processing cost with zero profit cut-off. The reporting cut-off was selected by the Competent Person following consideration of: · REE grade and basket composition; · metallurgical recovery; · enrichment in higher-value magnet and heavy rare earths; · permeability and transmissivity; · expected lixiviant consumption; · natural acid generation and acid consumption; · expected ISR wellfield configuration; · indicative operating costs; and · indicative rare earth product pricing. The Mineral Resource cut-off should therefore not be considered directly comparable with conventional excavation-based clay-hosted REE projects because the Wudinna Mineral Resource is being assessed for both extraction through ISR and open cut mining methods.

observations.scope: Assay data from air core drilling was omitted from grade estimation if Sonic core drilling presented, air core drilling was used for grade interpolation of flanks of the mineraliased bodies · The parent block dimensions were 50 m east × 50 m north × 1 m vertical, where required to adequately represent geological boundaries and mineralised horizons. · Block dimensions were selected with consideration of drillhole spacing, palaeochannel geometry, mineralised thickness and the anticipated scale of potential ISR wellfield development and open pit optimisation. · Variogram analysis was undertaken for individual REEs and principal estimation variables to characterise spatial continuity and establish appropriate estimation search parameters. · A multi-pass search strategy was applied in flattened model, with search distances and minimum and maximum sample and drillhole requirements selected to reflect observed geological and grade continuity and drillhole spacing. · Individual REEs were converted to oxides which were estimated separately and calculation of Total Rare Earth Oxide ("TREO"), Magnet Rare Earth Oxide ("MREO") and other reported REO groupings. Uranium and Thorium grades were estimated as deterous components. · Mineralised estimation domains were developed with consideration of geological continuity, REE grade distribution and the characteristics relevant to potential ISR recovery. · Model validation included visual comparison of input composites against estimated block grades, statistical comparison between composite sample grades and block model grades, Inverse Distance Squared estimation comparison with Ordinary Kriging, comparison volumes of block model and wireframes, SWATH analysis. No material conditional bias was identified from the validation procedures. · Previously MRE was not estimated, mining also was not performed Moisture · Whether the tonnages are estimated on a dry basis or with natural moisture, and the method of determination of the moisture content. · From 10.5 to 14.2%, average 13.3% Cut-off parameters · The basis of the adopted cut-off grade(s) or quality parameters applied. · The Mineral Resource is reported above a 200 ppm TREO-Ce for open pit method of mining and value of REO 5.27 US$ in individual operation ISR cell for covering of processing cost with zero profit cut-off. · The Mineral Resource cut-off should therefore not be considered directly comparable with conventional excavation-based clay-hosted REE projects because the Wudinna resource is being assessed for both extraction through ISR and open cut mining methods. · The Competent Person considers that the Mineral Resource as reported fulfills the reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction requirement for reporting Mineral Resources in accordance with the JORC Code.

observations.scope: The Mineral Resource cut-off should therefore not be considered directly comparable with conventional excavation-based clay-hosted REE projects because the Wudinna Mineral Resource is being assessed for both extraction through ISR and open cut mining methods. Mining method The conceptual mining method underlying the reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction assessment is in-situ recovery. ISR involves the controlled injection of a lixiviant into a permeable mineralised aquifer through injection wells.

Highlights ▪ Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) delivered for North Stanmore, establishing a ~20- year heavy rare earth development case with a post-tax NPV8 of A$1.21 billion, post-tax IRR of 240% and initial capital of A$155 million (including 30% contingency). ▪ Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5 years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion. ▪ Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO, underpinning 100% of the PFS production target. ▪ Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024 ppm TREO. ▪ Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006 hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore. ▪ Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent qualification. ▪ TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91% of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate. ▪ Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further high-grade material to the PFS mine plan. ▪ Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter. observations.scope: ASX ANNOUNCEMENT 30 October 2026 Quarterly Activities Report – 30 September 2026 Victory Metals (ASX:VTM) (Victory or the Company) is pleased to report on its activities and the Appendix 5B for the quarter ending 30 September 2026 (Quarter, Reporting Period). Highlights ▪ Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) delivered for North Stanmore, establishing a ~20- year heavy rare earth development case with a post-tax NPV8 of A$1.21 billion, post-tax IRR of 240% and initial capital of A$155 million (including 30% contingency). ▪ Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5 years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion. ▪ Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO, underpinning 100% of the PFS production target. ▪ Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024 ppm TREO. ▪ Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006 hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore. ▪ Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent qualification. ▪ TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91% of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate. ▪ Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further high-grade material to the PFS mine plan. ▪ Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter. observations.scope: ASX ANNOUNCEMENT 30 October 2026 Quarterly Activities Report – 30 September 2026 Victory Metals (ASX:VTM) (Victory or the Company) is pleased to report on its activities and the Appendix 5B for the quarter ending 30 September 2026 (Quarter, Reporting Period). Highlights ▪ Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) delivered for North Stanmore, establishing a ~20- year heavy rare earth development case with a post-tax NPV8 of A$1.21 billion, post-tax IRR of 240% and initial capital of A$155 million (including 30% contingency). ▪ Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5 years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion. ▪ Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO, underpinning 100% of the PFS production target. ▪ Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024 ppm TREO. ▪ Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006 hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore. ▪ Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent qualification. ▪ TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91% of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate. ▪ Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further high-grade material to the PFS mine plan. ▪ Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter. PFS, Maiden Ore Reserve and Updated Mineral Resource Establish 20-Year Development Case On 18 August 2026, Victory released the results of the North Stanmore Pre- Feasibility Study (PFS), a maiden Ore Reserve and an updated Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) for its 100%-owned North Stanmore Heavy Rare Earth Project near Cue, Western Australia.

of A$155 million (including 30% contingency). ▪ Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5 years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion. ▪ Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO, underpinning 100% of the PFS production target. ▪ Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024 ppm TREO. ▪ Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006 hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore. ▪ Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent qualification. ▪ TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91% of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate. ▪ Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further high-grade material to the PFS mine plan. ▪ Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter. observations.scope: Highlights ▪ Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) delivered for North Stanmore, establishing a ~20- year heavy rare earth development case with a post-tax NPV8 of A$1.21 billion, post-tax IRR of 240% and initial capital of A$155 million (including 30% contingency). ▪ Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5 years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion. ▪ Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO, underpinning 100% of the PFS production target. ▪ Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024 ppm TREO. ▪ Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006 hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore. ▪ Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent qualification. ▪ TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91% of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate. ▪ Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further high-grade material to the PFS mine plan. ▪ Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter. observations.scope: The first of four heap leach column cycles (~8 tonnes) was completed, generating ~5,000 L of Pregnant Leach Solution (PLS) at target leaching recovery rates. ▪ First PLS batch processed through the continuous precipitation circuit to produce a Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide (MREOH), marking the transition from rare earth extraction to a concentrated intermediate product. The MREOH will be refined into Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) samples for customer qualification (refer ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Plant Advances to Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production" 10 September 2026). ▪ The pilot campaign is generating the engineering and operating data required for Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) design which will commence early 2027. ▪ Mining Lease Application preparation continuing, with submission targeted for the end of 2026. Overland Project: carbonatite discovery extended ~5 km south with 130m intersection ▪ Niobium–rare earth carbonatite system identified at the R254 prospect: OV167 returned 19m @ 0.61% TREO from 86m to end of hole, including 7m @ 0.56% TREO with 0.27% Nb₂O₅ from 86m.

observations.scope: First Leach Cycle Complete: Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production Commenced The first of the four column cycles, using approximately 8 tonnes of ore, was completed during the quarter, generating continuous recovery of rare earths into approximately 5,000 L of Pregnant Leach Solution (PLS) at target leaching recovery rates (refer ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Plant Advances to Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production" 10 September 2026). The first batch of PLS was then processed through a continuous three-stage precipitation reactor to produce a Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide (MREOH), with full recoveries of rare earths from the PLS to the MREOH reported, in line with expectations. This step advanced the program beyond heap leaching into downstream product recovery, and marks the transition from demonstrating rare earth extraction to the start of producing a concentrated intermediate rare earth product.

observations.scope: The first of four heap leach column cycles (~8 tonnes) was completed, generating ~5,000 L of Pregnant Leach Solution (PLS) at target leaching recovery rates. ▪ First PLS batch processed through the continuous precipitation circuit to produce a Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide (MREOH), marking the transition from rare earth extraction to a concentrated intermediate product. The MREOH will be refined into Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) samples for customer qualification (refer ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Plant Advances to Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production" 10 September 2026). ▪ The pilot campaign is generating the engineering and operating data required for Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) design which will commence early 2027. ▪ Mining Lease Application preparation continuing, with submission targeted for the end of 2026. Overland Project: carbonatite discovery extended ~5 km south with 130m intersection ▪ Niobium–rare earth carbonatite system identified at the R254 prospect: OV167 returned 19m @ 0.61% TREO from 86m to end of hole, including 7m @ 0.56% TREO with 0.27% Nb₂O₅ from 86m.

observations.scope: First Leach Cycle Complete: Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production Commenced The first of the four column cycles, using approximately 8 tonnes of ore, was completed during the quarter, generating continuous recovery of rare earths into approximately 5,000 L of Pregnant Leach Solution (PLS) at target leaching recovery rates (refer ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Plant Advances to Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production" 10 September 2026).
